stories.description: Microsoft agreed to adopt guardrails and privacy standards for its AI in schools, as negotiated with the American Federation of Teachers.

stories.title: “We Think the Security Control Is Working” Is No Longer Good Enough
stories.description: Point-in-time audits and sampled assessments offer only snapshots; continuous control monitoring provides evidence that security controls are working today.

stories.title: KREMLIN Banking Malware Hijacks Chrome and Edge to Steal Credentials and Session Tokens
stories.description: KREMLIN targets Brazilian bank users with malicious Chrome and Edge extensions that steal credentials, session tokens, cookies, and browser data.

stories.title: CISA and NIST Release Technical Checklist for Safeguarding Identity Tokens From Theft and Misuse
stories.description: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) have released final technical guidance to stop attackers from forging, stealing, replaying, or misusing identity and access tokens.

stories.title: Iranian Hackers Use Telegram-Controlled Malware to Spy on Dissidents and Journalists
stories.description: U.S., U.K., and Dutch agencies say Iran’s intelligence service uses Telegram-controlled Windows malware to spy on dissidents and journalists.

stories.title: CISA Shares 17 Techniques Used by Hackers to Compromise Active Directory Environments
stories.description: CISA and five international cybersecurity agencies have released detailed guidance describing 17 common techniques hackers use to compromise Microsoft Active Directory environments.

stories.title: $1 Million Sandbox Challenge Uncovers Linux Kernel Flaws
stories.description: AI-assisted researchers flooded Vercel with reports, forcing the company to automate vulnerability triage.

stories.title: Apple Rolls Out Massive Security Update Fixing 273 Vulnerabilities Across Its Devices
stories.description: Apple has released one of its largest coordinated security rollouts, addressing 273 distinct critical vulnerabilities across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Vision Pro, Safari, and Xcode.
